body: NIST DLMF section 1.13 (Differential Equations) says: "A domain in the complex plane is simply-connected if it has no “holes”; more precisely, if its complement in the extended plane \mathbb{C}\cup\{\infty\} is connected. where z\in D , a simply-connected domain, and f(z) , g(z) are analytic in D , has an infinite number of analytic solutions in D . A solution becomes unique, for example, when w and \ifrac{\mathrm{d}w}{\mathrm{d}z} are prescribed at a point in D . Two solutions w_{1}(z) and w_{2}(z) are called a fundamental pair if any other solution w(z) is expressible as where A and B are constants. A fundamental pair can be obtained, for example, by taking any z_{0}\in D and requiring that The Wronskian of w_{1}(z) and w_{2}(z) is defined by (More generally \mathscr{W}\left\{w_{1}(z),\ldots,w_{n}(z)\right\}=\det\left[w_{k}^{(j-1)}(z)\right] , where 1\leq j,k\leq n .) Then the following relation is known as Abel’s identity where c is independent of z and f(z) is defined in ( 1.13.1 ). (More generally in ( 1.13.5 ) for n th-order differential equations, f(z) is the coefficient multiplying the (n-1) th-order derivative of the solution…" Equation 1.13.1 on the page has alt text "\frac{{\mathrm{d}}^{2}w}{{\mathrm{d}z}^{2}}+f(z)\frac{\mathrm{d}w}{\mathrm{d}z% }+g(z)w=0,". Equation 1.13.2 on the page has alt text "w(z)=Aw_{1}(z)+Bw_{2}(z),". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
